column2: Joshua's advanced days are stated in narrative and divine address, while much land still remains for inheritance.
Philistine, Geshurite and Canaanite territories introduce the remaining land, retaining all three selected groups.
The uninhabited region facing Egypt, Ekron and the left-side relation lead to five Philistine satrapies and the Hivites.
column3: The attachment of on the left of the Canaanites and the final Hivite clause is difficult; no simplified map or alternate boundary is substituted.

column2: Thaiman, Canaan opposite Gaza, Sidonians, Aphek and Amorite borders remain in the selected boundary sequence.
column3: The coordinated territorial and people descriptions continue the difficult preceding syntax; geographic identifications remain provisional.

column2: Gabli of the Philistines, eastern Lebanon, Gilgal beneath Hermon and Hamath's entrance remain, without substituting familiar parallel names.

Divine destruction is promised for the mountain inhabitants and Sidonians. Propose But distribute for Only distribute to preserve alla's contrast without making distribution Joshua's sole stated task.
Nine tribes plus half-Manasseh receive the land, and the selected longer clause explicitly makes the Great Sea the western boundary.
The two-and-a-half tribes' eastern grant repeats Moses gave it; the repetition is retained rather than treated as accidental duplication.
Aroer stands on Arnon's bank, a city lies in the ravine, and all Misor runs Medeba to Dibon; all three components remain.
Sihon's cities and Heshbon reign extend to Ammon's borders, preserving the royal description within the territorial list.
Gilead, Geshurite/Maacathite territories, all Hermon and all Bashan to Salcah remain in sequence.
Og rules from both Ashtaroth and Edrei, is among surviving giants, and is struck and destroyed by Moses.
The three undestroyed peoples include Canaanites; the ensuing residence clause explicitly names the king of Geshur and the Maacathites.
Levi's inheritance is the Lord Himself in the selected text, followed by the full Moses/Araboth-Moab/Jordan/Jericho division notice.
Reuben's grant is distributed by divisions, with inheritance supplied from the immediate allocation context.
Reuben's boundary begins at Aroer and includes the Arnon-ravine city and all Misor, retaining the repeated ravine designation.
Heshbon, Misor cities, Dibon, Bamoth-baal and the house of Beelmon are all retained; the house expression is not silently replaced by a different city form.
Jahaz, Kedemoth and Mephaath remain three successive entries in the allotment.
Kiriathaim, Sibmah, Serada and Sior on Mount Emak preserve the selected longer name sequence and mountain qualifier.
Beth-peor, Asedoth Phasga and Beth-jeshimoth remain separate entries without collapsing their inherited compound forms.
All Misor cities and Sihon's kingdom precede the five Midian rulers Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur and Reba, retaining their selected order.
column3: Inherited traditional Rekem/Reba represent selected Rokom/Robe here; their forms and order differ from Numbers 31:8 and are not claimed as an exhaustive name-authority resolution.

column2: Balaam son of Beor is explicitly the diviner and is killed in the onslaught.
column3: The force of en te rhope as onslaught is provisional and needs lexical review; no independent battle-mechanics claim is made.

column2: Jordan is named as Reuben's boundary before the repeated inheritance/divisions/cities/settlements summary.
Gad's grant follows the same divisions formula, preserving the repeated allocation introduction.
Jazer, all Gilead's cities and half Ammon's land extend to Aroer facing Rabbah; the half quantity remains.
Heshbon to Ramoth toward Mizpah, Betonim, Mahanaim and Debir's borders remain in the selected sequence.
column3: The relation of the Ramoth/Mizpah phrase and the final border endpoint remains a geographic-syntactic question.

column2: Emek's four named places, Sihon's remaining kingdom and Jordan's future boundary to part of Chinnereth remain.
Gad's inheritance is summarized by divisions, cities and settlements, without omitting the recurring formula.
Half-Manasseh's grant is also according to divisions, retaining the half-tribe qualification.
Mahanaim, Bashan's kingdom, Og's kingdom and Jair's villages retain their repetition, with sixty cities explicit.
Half Gilead, Ashtaroth and Edrei are assigned to the sons of Machir and to half those sons, preserving the difficult doubled beneficiary phrase.
column3: The selected whole/half Machir coordination is unresolved; no apparent redundancy is removed or silently corrected.

column2: Moses' beneficiaries are described with beyond the Jordan repeated, along with Araboth Moab and the east/opposite-Jericho position; no 13:33 is supplied.
The inheriting Israelites are distinguished from Eleazar, Joshua and the ancestral tribal leaders who assign the land.
The Lord commands through Joshua in the selected text, with nine and a half tribes and lot inheritance retained.
From beyond the Jordan remains the short continuation, followed by no Levitical lot; the missing longer allocation wording is not imported.
column3: The attachment of the opening phrase and the unexpressed giver's identity require fuller syntax review.

column2: Joseph's two tribes are Manasseh and Ephraim, while Levi receives cities and assigned land for livestock, followed by the repeated their livestock phrase.
column3: The final livestock coordination is syntactically awkward in the selected Greek and remains open rather than being silently deleted.

column2: Israel divides the land according to the Lord's command to Moses, preserving both agents.
Judah approaches at Gilgal and Caleb the Kenizzite addresses Joshua about the word concerning me and you at Kadesh-barnea.
Caleb was forty at the scouting mission and reported according to his mind, preserving the selected third-person possessor.
column3: The antecedent of autou is disputed; his mind is not changed to my mind or asserted to identify Moses conclusively. This carries forward the inherited dagger-note issue into the new evidence record.

column2: The other scouts turn away the people's heart, while Caleb gives himself to following the Lord my God.
The trodden land is promised to Caleb and his children for ever, with our God in Moses' quoted reason retained.
Forty-five years since the promise and age eighty-five agree with the earlier forty; sustained and the repeated now remain.
Caleb's current strength matches the time Moses sent him, expressed in going out and coming in for war.
The mountain request repeats that day, names current Anakim and fortified cities, and retains the condition if the Lord is with me.
Joshua blesses and grants Hebron to Caleb son of Jephunneh son of Kenaz, preserving the selected genealogy rather than substituting only an ethnic adjective.
The Kenizzite form returns here, and the continued Hebron grant is explained by following the Lord's command.
Hebron's former name is city of Arbok, the mother-city of the Anakim; no claim about an individual greatest man replaces the selected civic description.
